Daily Quiz.question: ১) Which character is not from Shakespeare’s tragedy “Hamlet”?
Daily Quiz.exp: Characters of William Shakespeare's tragedy ‘Hamlet’ are: Hamlet, Horatio, Ophelia, Claudius etc. Characters of William Shakespeare's tragedy 'Romeo and Juliet' are: Montague, Romeo, Juliet, Capulet. Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ২) Belial is a character from -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Belial, fictional character, a fallen angel in John Milton’s Paradise Lost (in 10 books, 1667; in 12 books, 1674) who tries to persuade the others to be more discreet so that their unacceptable behaviour is less conspicuous. The Hebrew word bĕlīyaʾal, apparently with the literal meaning “worthlessness,” was used in Old Testament epithets for the wicked and impious, such as the “sons of Belial.” In later traditions it was taken as a proper name, a byname for Satan.
Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ৩) Find the odd one out.
Daily Quiz.exp:
Characters of Three Musketeers are: Athos, Porthos, Aramis, D’Artagnan.
Characters of The Merchant of Venice are: Portia, Shylock.
Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) Which character is from the novel ‘Moby Dick’?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Captain Ahab, fictional character, a one-legged captain of the whaling vessel Pequod in the novel Moby Dick (1851), by Herman Melville.
Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ৫) The fictional character ‘Fitzwilliam Darcy’ is created by -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Fitzwilliam Darcy, fictional character, the suitor of Elizabeth Bennet in the novel Pride and Prejudice (1813) by Jane Austen. At first Elizabeth spurns him because of his extreme pride, but when Darcy and Elizabeth come to know one another, his true character is revealed.
Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ৬) Which one is a monstrous creature?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Grendel, fictional character, a monstrous creature defeated by Beowulf in the Old English poem Beowulf (composed between 700 and 750 CE).
Gollum, fictional character in J.R.R. Tolkien’s novels The Hobbit (1937) and The Lord of the Rings (1954–55). Gollum is a vaguely reptilian creature who is obsessed with the ring that is the focus of much of the action of the books.
Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ৭) Which is not a character from Daniel Defoe’s ‘Robinson Crusoe’?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Characters of Robinson Crusoe are: Robinson Crusoe, Friday, Xury.
Characters of Arms and the Man are: Captain Bluntschli, Raina, Louka, Nicola.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

Daily Quiz.question: ৮) Macbeth was beheaded by -
Daily Quiz.exp: King Duncan, Macbeth, Macduff, Lady Macbeth, Malcolm and Three Witches are the important characters of Shakespeare's play ‘Macbeth’. Macbeth was beheaded by Macduff. Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) Which character is not from Homer’s Iliad?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Ariel is a character from Shakespeare’s swan song ‘The Tempest’. Helen, Achilles, Paris, Thetis, Nestor, Hector are from Homer’s ‘Iliad’.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) “Belinda” - is character from -
Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) The Rape of the Lock
Daily Quiz.exp:
Belinda, Baron, Ariel - These are the characters taken from the mock heroic epic - The Rape of the Lock by Alexander Pope.
Source: LiveMCQ Archive

Daily Quiz.question: ১১) Antipholus of Ephesus- is a character from Shakespeare’s which play?
Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) To Be or Not To Be
Daily Quiz.exp:
Egeon, Antipholus of Syracuse, Antipholus of Ephesus, Dromio, Emilia -- etc are the characters of The Comedy of Errors.
Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ১২) Cornelius is a character from Christopher Marlowe’s -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Characters of Christopher Marlowe’s Dr. Faustus are: Dr. Faustus, Cornelius, Mephistopheles etc.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

Daily Quiz.question: ১৩) Which one is a character from ‘The Canterbury Tales’?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Harry Bailly, Bailly also spelled Bailey, fictional character, the genial and outspoken host of the Tabard Inn who accompanies the group of pilgrims to Canterbury in Geoffrey Chaucer’s The Canterbury Tales (c. 1387–1400). Mr. Barkis is a character from Charles Dickens’ David Copperfield.
Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ১৪) Estella is a character from___
Daily Quiz.option3: গ) A Tale Of Two Cities
Daily Quiz.exp:
Abel Magwitch, Pip, Estella, Miss Havisham, Mr Jaggers are the important characters of Charles Dickens’ Great Expectations.
Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ১৫) 'Desdemona' is an important character in the Shakespearean play -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Othello, a Moorish general in the service of Venice in Shakespeare’s Othello. Driven by jealousy that has been skillfully manipulated, Othello takes the life of Desdemona, his doting wife, and then his own.
Source: britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) In order to avoid being robbery targets, tourists are encouraged to not wear _____ jewelry.
Daily Quiz.exp:
Ostentatious (adjective) - Intended to attract admiration or notice; দৃষ্টি-আকর্ষক, জাঁকালো।
Synonyms: Pretentious, Conspicuous, Flamboyant. Antonyms: Plain, Unobtrusive, Restrained, Modest.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৭) Antonym of ‘Meddling’ -
Daily Quiz.exp: Officious (adjective) - Too eager to tell people what to do and having too high an opinion of your own importance. Synonyms: Interfering, Intrusive, Meddling. Antonyms: Self-effacing.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৮) Since I do not have a law degree, I find it hard to understand the _____ terms of the contract.
Daily Quiz.exp: Recondite (adjective) - জটিল, দুর্বোধ্য; Not known about by many people and difficult to understand. Synonyms: Complex, Abstruse, Complicated. Antonyms: Straightforward, Simple, Familiar.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৯) Insolent or impertinent behavior -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Effrontery [noun] [Uncountable noun] - Insolent or impertinent behavior
Synonyms: Shamelessness, Impoliteness, Disrespect. Antonyms: Timidity.

Daily Quiz.question: ২০) Antonym of ‘Whimsical’ -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Whimsical (adjective) - Unusual and strange in a way that might be funny or annoying.
Synonyms: Mischievous, Eccentric, Peculiar. Antonyms: Hardheaded, Logical, Reasonable.

Daily Quiz.question: ২১) Which is not a synonym for ‘Denigrate’?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Denigrate (verb transitive) - মানহানি, কালিমালেপন করা; Synonyms: Diminish, Insult, Revile. Antonyms: Extol.
Incite - প্ররোচিত করা।

Daily Quiz.question: ২২) Incite অর্থ -
Daily Quiz.exp: Foment (verb transitive) - প্ররোচিত করা, উত্তেজিত করা; To cause something bad or illegal to develop. Synonyms: Incite, Provoke, Encourage (উৎসাহিত করা). Antonyms: Calm, Restrain, Tranquilize.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৩) Deference এর অর্থ -
Daily Quiz.exp: Deference (noun) [uncountable noun] - শ্রদ্ধাবোধ, শিষ্টাচার, সৌজন্য; Respect shown for another person especially because of that person’s experience, knowledge, age, or power. Synonyms: Respect, Courtesy, Politeness, Antonyms: Disrespect.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৪) Because of her shyness, Lori would often ____ herself in doing chores in the kitchen while everyone else enjoyed the party.
Daily Quiz.exp: Relegate (verb transitive) - অপসারিত করা, নিম্নপদস্থ করা; To put something or someone into a lower or less important rank or position. Synonyms: Downgrade, Lower, Degrade. Antonyms: Upgrade, Promote.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৫) Antonym of ‘Straightforward’ -
Daily Quiz.exp: Convoluted (participial adjective) - জটিল, হিতবুদ্ধিকর; Having a complicated structure and therefore difficult to understand. Synonyms: Complex, Puzzling, Perplexing. Antonyms: Simple, Straightforward..

Daily Quiz.question: ২৬) Opposite of ‘Tacit’ -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Tacit (adjective) - চাপা, উহ্য, মনে মনে; Understood without being expressed directly.
Synonyms: Implicit, Implied, Unspoken. Antonyms: পরিষ্কারভাবে বলা; Explicit, Stated.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৭) Without preamble he began talking. Here ‘Preamble’ is a/an -
Daily Quiz.exp: Preamble (noun) - প্রারম্ভিক মন্তব্য, উপস্থাপনা, ভূমিকা। Synonyms: Introduction, Foreword, Prelude. Antonyms: Epilogue.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৮) ‘To replace something older, less effective, or less important’ is the meaning of which word?
Daily Quiz.exp: Supersede (verb transitive) - To replace something older, less effective, or less important or official; প্রতিস্থাপন করা, অপসারিত করা। Synonyms: Replace, Supplant, Override. Antonyms: Keep, Retain, Stay.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৯) His arguments were <u>well suited to the circumstances</u>, and his choice of language was the theme of constant admiration. Replace the underlined part with a suitable word.
Daily Quiz.exp:
Felicitous (adjective) - যথাযথ, উপযোগী, প্রাসঙ্গিক; Well chosen or suited to the circumstances.
Synonyms: Suitable, Appropriate, Relevant. Antonyms: Inappropriate, Unfortunate.

Daily Quiz.question: ৩০) ‘Precarious’ means -
Daily Quiz.exp: Precarious (adjective) - আত্মবিশ্বাসহীন, অনিরাপদ, ঝুকিপূর্ণ ; In danger because not firmly fixed; likely to fall or suffer harm. Synonyms: Insecure, Unreliable, Risky. Antonyms: Safe, Secure.
